title: Bookmark Method Standard Setting for AI Safety Benchmarks

original_idea.body:
# Bookmark Method Standard Setting for AI Safety Benchmarks: Using Ordered Item Booklet Methodology to Set Defensible Performance Level Descriptors

**Problem:** AI safety benchmarks lack formal Performance Level Descriptors (PLDs)—descriptions of what a model at each safety level actually does and does not do. Without PLDs, safety grades (e.g., 'Low Risk,' 'High Risk') are labels without behavioral content. The Bookmark method provides a structured procedure for deriving PLDs from expert judgment about item difficulty ordering.

**Direction:** Implement the Bookmark method for a safety benchmark: (1) Order items by their IRT-estimated difficulty (probability that a model of any given safety level answers correctly). (2) Create an Ordered Item Booklet (OIB) presenting items from easiest to hardest. (3) Have a panel of AI safety experts 'bookmark' the location where the transition from one performance level to the next occurs. (4) Average bookmarks across panelists to set the cutoff. (5) Develop PLDs describing what models at each level do. (6) Compare Bookmark-derived cutoffs to Angoff-derived cutoffs and current ad hoc thresholds.

**Why it matters:** The Bookmark method is the most widely used alternative to Angoff for high-stakes standard setting and has shown superior validity in medical education (BMC Medical Education 2020). It produces not just cutoffs but interpretable descriptions of what each performance level means—critical for regulatory communication. An OIB requires IRT difficulty estimates plus expert judgment, with no heavy coding required.

**Relevant context:** Bookmark vs. Angoff comparison studies show Bookmark produces higher validity indices (BMC Medical Education 2020). The Bookmark method is used for NAEP, ACCUPLACER, and other high-stakes assessments. R packages for IRT difficulty estimation (eRm, mirt, TAM) provide the necessary inputs. AI safety benchmarks lack formal PLDs that could guide deployment decisions. No published work applies Bookmark methodology to AI safety evaluation.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: lack of PLDs means safety grades are labels without behavioral content, undermining deployment decisions. Bookmark-derived PLDs make safety levels interpretable, directly improving regulatory communication and deployment decisions.

low_compute.reasoning: IRT difficulty estimation in R plus expert panel judgment. Minimal compute, CPU-only.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: The Bookmark method is conceptually accessible (order items, have experts place bookmarks). IRT calibration for difficulty ordering is intermediate. Panel logistics add non-technical complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Requires IRT calibration, creating ordered item booklet, recruiting and running expert panel, and developing PLDs. Panel logistics make this a sustained multi-week effort even for one benchmark.

quick_reasoning: Targets a specific, well-defined AI safety governance problem (setting defensible performance level descriptors) with clear Bookmark methodology using IRT; scope is precise and directly actionable.
